history.period: 14th-15th century (per Lower Dibang Valley district site); one government tourist circuit page says 12th century
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed: Rukmini Nati is the ruins of a brick hill-fort/palace at the heart of Chimiri (Chimri) village, about 12 km from Roing - remains of burnt and baked bricks, with 1972-73 excavations exposing a two-room brick structure (10 m x 10 m x 12 m) up to plinth level. Legend holds it was the palace of Princess Rukmini, daughter of King Bhismak. DATE CONFLICT (verify): roing.nic.in tourism page says 14th/15th century; the district's tourist-packages page says 12th century AD. IDENTITY CONFLICT: one travel guide (delhitravel.org) describes it as an ancient cave temple dedicated to Goddess Rukmini - this appears to be a confusion with the separate Kupunli cave temple near Hunli; the government source describes only fort/palace ruins.

name: Rukmini Nati (Chimiri Fort)
town_description: Roing is the headquarters of Lower Dibang Valley district in eastern Arunachal Pradesh, on the banks of the Dibang river. It is the gateway town for the Dibang Valley circuit, Bhismaknagar ruins, Mehao Lake and Mayudia.
tradition: Archaeological site (ruined hill-fort/palace; not a temple)

travel.airport: Dibrugarh Airport (Assam), about 100-120 km; Tezu Airport (TEI) has limited scheduled flights.
travel.railway: Tinsukia Junction (Assam), about 90-100 km away, is the nearest major railhead.
travel.road: At Chimiri village, about 12 km north of Roing by road.

visitor_information.best_time: October to April, the dry season around Roing.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open ruins with no fixed hours; visit in daylight (verify locally).
